from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Mapping Concept", 
                          ["Linear transformations map between vector spaces.", 
                           "An m by n matrix defines this mapping.", 
                           "We move from n dimensions to m dimensions."])
        
        # Objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        vec_v = Vector([1, 2], color="#FF5733")
        label_v = MathTex(r"\\vec{v}", color="#FF5733").next_to(vec_v.get_end(), UP)
        
        matrix_m = MathTex(r"M = \\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\\\ 0 & 1 \\end{pmatrix}", color="#33FF57")
        
        vec_mv = Vector([1.5, 1], color="#3357FF")
        label_mv = MathTex(r"M\\vec{v}", color="#3357FF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(axes)
        self.play(Create(vec_v), Write(label_v))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_m, 'A5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_m))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(label_mv, 'C4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Create(vec_mv), Write(label_mv))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#3357FF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Geometry of the Kernel and Image", 
                          ["Compression loses information permanently.", 
                           "Different inputs can yield the same output.", 
                           "This space of loss is the kernel."])
        
        # Objects
        # Kernel: A line
        kernel = Line(start=LEFT*1.5, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#FF4500", stroke_width=6)
        # Image: A plane
        image = Polygon(UL, UR, DR, DL, color="#32CD32", fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Assets
        camera_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/camera.svg").set_color("#FF4500")
        doc_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/document.svg").set_color("#1E90FF")
        
        # Positioning based on feedback (VideoCritic)
        self.place_at_grid(kernel, "B4", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(image, "E4", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(camera_icon, "B3", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # Transformation map indicator
        arrow = Arrow(kernel.get_center(), image.get_center(), color="#1E90FF", buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(doc_icon, "D5", scale_factor=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.play(Create(kernel), FadeIn(camera_icon))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.play(Create(image))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#1E90FF"))
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow), FadeIn(doc_icon))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Real-world Application", [
            "Matrices drive data science applications.", 
            "Expand data for better analysis.", 
            "Compress data for efficient storage."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        server_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/server.svg", color="#FF69B4")
        harddrive_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/harddrive.svg", color="#FFA500")

        network_nodes = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, fill_opacity=0.8, color=WHITE) for _ in range(5)])
        
        for i, node in enumerate(network_nodes):
            self.place_at_grid(node, ["B2", "B4", "C1", "C3", "C5"][i])
        self.place_at_grid(server_icon, "D2", scale_factor=0.3)
            
        network_group = VGroup(network_nodes, server_icon)
        
        edges = VGroup(*[Line(network_nodes[i].get_center(), network_nodes[j].get_center(), stroke_width=2) 
                         for i, j in [(0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 3), (2, 4)]])
        
        # Use an animation container as requested by criticism 34
        animation_container = VGroup(network_group, edges)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(animation_container))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF69B4"))
        self.play(network_group.animate.set_color("#FF69B4"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        signal = Dot(color="#7FFF00")
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#7FFF00"))
        self.add(signal)
        for i in range(len(edges)):
            self.play(MoveAlongPath(signal, edges[i]), run_time=0.5)
        self.remove(signal)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        result_box = harddrive_icon
        self.place_at_grid(result_box, "D5", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFA500"))
        self.play(Create(result_box), FadeOut(animation_container))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Geometric Interpretation of Non-Square Matrices as Dimensional Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresher: The Mapping Concept
sections.content: Briefly define a linear transformation as a mapping between vector spaces. Remind students that an m x n matrix represents a transformation from n-dimensional space to m-dimensional space.
sections.example: Visualizing a 2D arrow (vector) being transformed by a matrix into a new position.

sections.title: Expanding Dimensions (m > n): The 'Projection' Perspective
sections.content: Explain how an m x n matrix (where m > n) embeds a lower-dimensional space into a higher-dimensional space. Visualize this as placing a 2D sheet of paper into 3D space.
sections.example: A 2D character (a cat) moving inside a 3D room. The matrix maps the cat's local 2D coordinates onto specific 3D floor coordinates.

sections.title: Compressing Dimensions (m < n): The 'Shadow' Perspective
sections.content: Discuss dimensionality reduction. When m < n, the transformation 'squashes' information, effectively creating a projection or 'shadow' of the high-dimensional data.
sections.example: Using a light source to cast the shadow of a 3D dinosaur figure onto a 2D flat wall. The matrix acts as the 'light' that simplifies the 3D data into 2D.

sections.title: The Geometry of the Kernel and Image
sections.content: Explain the concept of 'loss of information.' Emphasize that when compressing (m < n), multiple inputs can map to the same output, creating a 'kernel' (a null space) that represents the collapsed dimensions.
sections.example: Several different 3D 'lego' structures casting the exact same 2D silhouette on a wall, demonstrating that the 3D depth information was lost in the transformation.

sections.title: Synthesis & Real-world Application
sections.content: Conclude by summarizing that non-square matrices are the engines of data processing—either expanding data for analysis (feature engineering) or compressing it for storage/visualization (PCA).
sections.example: A robotic arm (device) with 3 sensors (3D) sending data to a controller that processes it into 2 motor commands (2D) to navigate a path.
